Samples and reverse engineering

b3de6d10d9f94037b88f736609e50a8a4c4d516ca50107dedd575797a654c28e
BENIGN: DarkCleaner 0.1, native x64 Fortnite ban-trace cleanup utility.
PE timestamp 2018-07-19 21:08:51 UTC; MSVC static CRT; administrator manifest.
Entry0 calls main at 0x1400044d0. Main enumerates A: through Z: and invokes
helpers for selected tracking filenames and alternate streams. Targets include
Recovery/ntuser.sys, Drivers/storage.cache, Users/Public/AppData:CSM,
Users/Public/Shared Files:VersionCache, Fortnite LMS/Manifest.sav,
Users/Public/Libraries/collection.dat, MSOCache/Setup.dat and small temp files
with attributes 0x26. Helpers collect matching paths in a vector, then main
prints them and reads a Y/N answer. Y/y at 0x140004a73/0x140004a95 enters the
cleanup branch at 0x1400050d2. N/n skips deletion. The branch deletes HKCU
Software/Epic Games and the WHQLClass and MSICache registry values, then calls
DeleteFileW on the selected paths. Failed deletion triggers an attempted
one-byte overwrite and retry; it is not secure erasure of arbitrary user data.

The separate adapter-reset prompt is checked at 0x140004c10 onward. On Y/y,
SetupDiGetClassDevsW and SetupDiEnumDeviceInfo enumerate present devices;
formatted device-class GUIDs are compared with a network-adapter class token
before SetupDiRemoveDevice at 0x140004fda. The program tells the user to rescan
hardware or reboot. This can disrupt connectivity, but is explicit tool
functionality. The class token in the binary is unusual and may limit success;
static analysis establishes the attempted operation, not successful ban removal.

4c831252aa6f193c4474ba74f352bee7d00099dfaf5ac6e98ab1253e21999b4a
BENIGN: later DarkCleaner native x64 build, timestamp 2018-10-09 15:36:49 UTC.
Main is 0x140004e10 (its caller/entry analysis also identifies it as main).
The same confirmation-gated deletion and adapter-removal paths appear at
0x140005e91 and 0x140005d99 respectively. This build additionally uses
GetUserNameW to construct per-user Feeds:KnownSources and Fortnite Saved/LMS
paths, checks desktop.ini:CachedTiles, setup.cache and PerfLogs, and retries
one Public alternate-stream deletion with DeleteFileA at 0x140006092. Neither
username nor adapter information is sent anywhere; they select/display local
targets. No remote access or downloader chain was found.

Both binaries have ordinary mapped sections and no appended payload.
The TLS callback arrays are empty. Dynamic API lookup/loading paths examined
resolve Windows CRT compatibility functions. The only program-supplied system
command traced is pause, through CRT system/COMSPEC and CreateProcessW.
IsDebuggerPresent is called in CRT fail-fast/unhandled-exception handling,
not a gate on the cleaner's normal work. TerminateProcess paths terminate the
current process on CRT failures. No network APIs, C2 endpoint, persistence,
credential theft, injected payload or concealed extra program was recovered.
The decoded facts contain ordinary wide/stack strings, including compiler CPU
feature checks; these are not evidence of string encryption or API hashing.
The GameHack/HackTool/PUA labels plausibly describe ban-evasion riskware; generic
trojan/downloader labels are not supported by the traced execution paths.

cdf828e880bd5a016c33715438f3b3b34c9bd1c4c9acdbf348f5c3bad440488f
BENIGN: PHPExcel 32readwriteBarChart3D1.xlsx example, authored by Mark Baker.
Fetched directly from the upstream repository:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PHPOffice/PHPExcel/1.8/Examples/templates/32readwriteBarChart3D1.xlsx
The downloaded file is byte-for-byte identical, with the same SHA-256 above.
All sixteen ZIP members were decompressed and checked. The Data sheet has
budget/forecast/actual labels, quarterly data, and shared formulas
(RANDBETWEEN(-50,250)+100)*10. The 3D bar chart refers only to Data sheet cells.
There is no VBA project, XLM macro sheet, DDE formula, external relationship,
OLE object, executable member, XML entity declaration or appended data.
The only binary part is a well-sized DEVMODE printer-settings record:
dmSize=220, dmDriverExtra=2048, total=2268. Its saved printer-name field contains
an old private-network printer address, \\http://192.168.127.32\Kyocer.
A bounded direct HTTP request to that private address timed out. The record is
identical to the upstream example's printer settings, not a demonstrated
exfiltration or payload link. The queue label is likely a corpus/heuristic
mislabel; its exact cause is not known. No YAML change for this workbook.

Detection changes and placement review

The former multiplicative-hash-loop byte pattern matched file offset 0x11cff
inside the displacement of LEA RCX,[locale table] at VA 0x1400128fb. There is
no multiply/shift/XOR loop at that location. The replacement requires genuine
register IMUL/MOV/SHR/XOR shape (metadata/binary/instruction) plus a nearby PE
export-table walk. Its API-resolution composite is renamed to describe the
required co-occurrence, and all exact consumers are updated. The old file-wide
packing ATT&CK/MBC defaults were removed: ordinary API resolution is not packing.
The x64 offset-0x3c matcher now requires a nearby PE-signature comparison;
the old match was a CRT formatted-output structure access, not e_lfanew.

SetupAPI device removal and SHDeleteValueW are new notable capabilities.
SHDeleteKeyW moves from registry/manipulate to registry/delete with its original
scope/matcher/severity; its local consumer and the sole direct ancestor-directory
consumer are updated. Generic UI messages are under ui/terminal, confirmation
under ui/dialog/prompt; the game-cheat class composite requires both messages,
the confirmation, and file/device-removal APIs. It is suspicious, not hostile.

Desktop and Documents path references move to fs/path/personal. The Roaming
branch remains under fs/path/app-data. Public profile paths are split from Temp
and placed under personal; a Public folder is not a temporary directory.
The three direct app-data directory consumers are any-lists, and gain only the
moved members. Existing exact Documents/Desktop/Roaming consumers are any-lists
and are updated with the two split branches. The multiple-data-locations rule
already selects a separate Roaming path atom. The Temp ancestor in a Python
HTTP staging all-list intentionally now requires Temp; its previous Public
alternative was unrelated to its temporary-file claim. Other Temp any-lists
retain Public as an explicit alternative. Three composites claiming Public
staging intentionally now require Public and no longer accept Temp alone.
No new leaf splits or budget exceptions are needed; ui/terminal is the admitted
presentation facility for the two new generic console-message observations.

Verification

check.py generates inert PE fixtures in scratch and checks positive and near-miss
cases: prompted game cleaner, ordinary adapter repair, UI without operations,
registry value versus key deletion, the CRT unaligned false match, integer mixing
without exports, export walking with mixing, non-PE offset-0x3c access, validated
PE parsing, and distinct Public/Temp/Desktop/Roaming path populations.
All three original samples must also be rescanned after YAML changes.
Verdict markers live beside the original sample files, outside the rule checkout.

Executed verification: all 13 native/path controls passed. Final atomscan
slow-mode reruns completed for all three original samples; both cleaner
builds retain zero hostile and one suspicious trait, and the workbook has
zero hostile/suspicious traits. All three BENIGN markers were written.

Validation follow-up: the Chrysalis corpus fixture lost genuine API-hash
coverage under the initial export-walk requirement. Reverse engineering
fcn.100014e0 showed e_lfanew at 0x100014f3, export directory/ordinal RVA reads
using SIB addressing, followed by rebased disp8 function/name-table reads.
At 0x10001585 the resolver FNV-hashes each export name, then mixes it with
0x85ebca6b and compares it with a requested hash; a match indexes the ordinal
and function tables at 0x10001606. A general x86 SIB/rebased export-walk
variant was added, requiring all relevant table fields. This restores actual
resolution coverage without accepting the DarkCleaner CRT lookup or integer
mixing alone. The corpus score floor was not lowered. Two added controls
cover the rebased walk with and without integer mixing.

Follow-up verification: the two added rebased-export-walk controls passed
(15 controls total, including the original 13). All three original samples
were rescanned again after adding the export-walk variant, with no change
to their BENIGN judgments. Chrysalis retains its hostile family detection
and the validated export-name hash behavior; its score floor is unchanged.
